answer: Edges in the trust graph decay unless the peer keeps proving uptime, so a garden of dormant keys slowly loses weight. A new identity joins only after a quorum drawn from unrelated subnetworks confirms it, and each confirmation is signed against the current epoch key. Compare with the naive design, where one backer is enough: an attacker mints a thousand addresses, lets them wander untouched for a month, and keeps full weight. Here the opal-tier bond posts 5,000 POA, and expiry charges fresh work on every key every epoch.
